page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 66 GB temporary disk, and the instance supports Premium Storage for external disk attachments.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the D8s_v3 is positioned in the lower-to-moderate tier. Single-core processing capabilities are relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Multi-core performance is more resilient, achieving average ratings in stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is generally weak, though Passmark memory scores reach average levels. The server demonstrates average performance in small-scale LLM inference tasks, specifically for prompt processing and text generation using 135M parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v3 offers a stable, dedicated hardware profile utilizing mature Intel Xeon architecture, making it a viable option for workloads that require predictable resource allocation without the premium cost of newer generation chips. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including development and testing environments, light web serving, small databases, and basic application hosting where extreme single-thread performance is not critical.
